fullText:
Laptops, phones and documents seized as information commissioner acts on messages about mis-selling scandal

Laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized after officials carried out search warrants in a crackdown on claims companies plaguing people with spam text messages about the car finance mis-selling scandal.

The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) executed warrants at homes and businesses linked to five companies in London, Liverpool, Bolton, Burnley and Swansea on Wednesday.

More than 12m complaints about nuisance marketing text messages have been submitted by the public since September 2025 as claims management companies (CMCs) and other firms attempt to grab a share of the billions of pounds in compensation expected to be paid out to motorists who were mis-sold car loans.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) announced a £7.5bn industry-wide compensation scheme for the millions of victims of the scandal in March.

Legal challenges, however, forced the regulator to partly suspend the scheme.

The FCA had expected to start paying out £829 on average this year to those affected by the scandal – in which drivers were overcharged for loans as a result of commission payments between lenders and car dealers between 2007 and 2024 – but a court ordered the regulator to suspend parts of the scheme until a hearing in December or February next year.

The head of investigations at the ICO, Andy Curry, said: “People are fed up with being bombarded by unwanted calls, texts and emails about car finance claims, and we’re taking action.”

This week’s raids “send a clear message to the claims management sector: comply with the law or expect to hear from us”, he said.

The companies linked to the searches are subject to continuing investigation. They are believed to be responsible for sending a combined 170m texts to members of the public between September 2025 and May this year.

The ICO is working with the FCA, the Advertising Standards Authority and the Solicitors Regulation Authority to tackle poor practices relating to motor finance claims by some CMCs, law firms and lead generation companies.

The raids represent an escalation of the crackdown on rogue CMCs and other businesses. As a result of the FCA’s work, more than 1,200 misleading adverts have been removed or amended since January 2024.

Some firms face enforcement investigations, while others have had to reduce their “unreasonable” fees or allow consumers to walk away from contracts free of charge.

The ICO has the power to apply to the courts for a warrant to search premises as part of investigations under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations, where evidence may be seized. This can include mobile phones, laptops and sim farms: collections of devices that house hundreds or thousands of mobile phone sim cards.

The FCA has said there is no need to use a CMC or law firm because people can complain for free using a template letter on its website. This week it launched a nationwide advertising campaign to direct people to the letter. It will run across TV, radio, print, billboards and social media until 6 September.

title: 'Time for change is now' - MVP and PFL merge
description: Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League merge to create "a combat sports company for the new era".
fullText:
Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League have merged to create "a combat sports company for the new era".

The newly formed partnership will be led by MVP co-founders Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, with PFL head John Martin also on the board and continuing to operate as CEO.

The PFL will move under the brand of MVP to bring together a roster of more than 300 fighters across boxing and mixed martial arts (MMA).

MVP focused on boxing when launching in 2021 but ventured into MMA for the first time in May.

"We started MVP to disrupt a broken model," Paul said.

"We wanted to give fighters fair pay and a bigger, modernised stage to become global superstars. Joining forces with PFL accelerates that vision by a decade.

"To all current MVP and PFL fighters, things just got bigger. To fighters fighting in other organisations, we are open for business when you are contractually free. The time for change is now."

MVP's first - and only - MMA show set a new record for the most-watched MMA event in the United States, with a "minute audience" of 12.4 million viewers as Ronda Rousey beat Gina Carrano, according to broadcaster Netflix.

Rousey's 15-second win peaked at 17 million viewers globally on Netflix, shattering the previous record of nine million.

The PFL has attempted to innovate the MMA space since launching in 2017, opting for a league-based system with points gained in each fight before season-ending play-offs.

It initially offered prize money of $1m (£750,000) but made sweeping changes in 2025 and reduced that to $500,000 (£374,000).

"Over the past seven years, PFL has built the world's number two global MMA company," Martin said.

"We're not just combining companies, we're bringing an entire combat sports community together and creating a more powerful platform to accelerate growth.

"One company, one global stage, millions of fans - and we're only just getting started."

It comes after MVP announced a new partnership with Matchroom Boxing on Tuesday, with the aim of creating more opportunities for female fighters across both promotional rosters.

MVP has invested heavily in women's boxing over the past five years and boasts an impressive stable of world champions, including Britons Caroline Dubois and Chantelle Cameron.

title: Premier League clubs agree EFL funding proposal
description: Premier League clubs agreed a funding proposal that they will put to the EFL over the next few days.
fullText:
An end is finally in sight to the long-running funding dispute between the Premier League and the English Football League.

The Premier League confirmed its 20 clubs have "unanimously voted" to approve a proposal for a "new strategic partnership", which will be put to the EFL for its members to vote on in the next few days.

No figure has been put on the deal, which is due to last 10 years, with both sides keen not to debate the issue in public.

The Premier League says the proposal is fully funded. It is expected to come through a transfer levy.

"The Premier League already has long-term funding commitments to invest a record £1.6billion every three years into the wider game and communities," said the Premier League.

"The Premier League remains committed to finding a football-led solution and looks forward to continuing discussions with the EFL on progressing this proposal."

'Clock ticking' on financial stand-off - regulator

The funding row has been rumbling on since a fan-led review in 2021, which was commissioned by the government following a number of crises in the sport, including the failed European Super League project and the collapse of Bury FC.

On a number of occasions, it has seemed a deal was close. In March 2024, the Premier League was warned by government officials that if it and the EFL failed to agree a deal, one would be imposed on them.

On Tuesday, representatives of the Premier League, the EFL and the new Independent Regulator met to discuss the outline of a deal.

"The EFL notes the Premier League's position following its meeting with clubs earlier today, and now looks forward to receiving its formal proposal for consideration," said the EFL.

"This follows constructive discussions involving the EFL, Premier League and Independent Football Regulator over recent months.

"The EFL Board will then review the full detail of the proposal, including its potential benefits, implications and alignment with the long-term interests of our 72 clubs, ahead of further dialogue with the Premier League.

"The proposal will then be discussed in detail with our member clubs to determine next steps."

Resistance within the Premier League simply to hand over money was based on a number of factors, including the basic reality they would providing funds to clubs trying to replace them.

In other instances, specifically Stoke City, EFL clubs have owners richer than some in the Premier League.

title: Wu edges past Murphy into Shanghai semi-finals
description: World champion Wu Yize overcomes "a lot of mistakes" to edge past Shaun Murphy 6-5 and reach the Shanghai Masters semi-finals.
fullText:
World champion Wu Yize overcame "a lot of mistakes" to edge past Shaun Murphy 6-5 and reach the Shanghai Masters semi-finals.

Meeting for the first time since Wu won the dramatic World Championship final in May, the 22-year-old trailed by five frames to four in the third round, having led 3-1, before building his fifth 50-plus break of the match to force a decider.

After England's Murphy unexpectedly missed a red when leading 62-29 in the final frame, the Chinese held his nerve to clear the black and complete another nail-biting win.

Wu will face England's Judd Trump in the last four after he brushed aside Scotland's John Higgins 6-0, including three consecutive century breaks in the final three frames.

"Although the result was good and I managed to win the match, I never really took control of it. Hopefully I can find my rhythm and get back to my best in the next match as I prepare for the semi-finals," said Wu.

"I definitely made a lot of mistakes that I shouldn't have made. To be honest, I didn't expect to get another chance in the deciding frame, and I was quite surprised when Shaun missed and let me in.

"I don't think either of us played particularly well today. It wasn't as high a standard as the match we produced in the World Championship final."

Defending champion Kyren Wilson recovered from 5-3 down to beat three-time world champion Mark Williams in a deciding frame, reeling off breaks of 61, 54 and 113 to complete his comeback.

He will face 2025 world champion Zhao Xintong in a repeat of last year's semi-final, which Wilson won 10-5.

Zhao crushed Australia's Neil Robertson 6-0, with a highest break of 117 in the third frame.

title: Littler's nan shocked by seeing mural from bus
description: A mural in Warrington honouring two-time world darts champion Luke Littler surprises his grandmother after she spots it while on a local bus.
fullText:
A mural in Warrington honouring two-time world darts champion Luke Littler left his grandmother shocked after she spotted it while on a local bus.

Littler, 19, watched on Thursday as the mural, placed on the side of Golden Square Shopping Centre, was unveiled.

But on Wednesday, Littler's grandmother was on a bus that passed the mural as it was being prepared for the ceremony. She got off to look at it before contacting other members of the family.

"I think my nan was on the bus yesterday," said Littler, speaking to BBC Sport's Nesta McGregor. "She actually came down here, she got off the bus and spoke to the guys that were doing it. Then, she phoned my dad and that's how I found out.

"She was here before us. Unbelievable. I think that was always going to happen really.

"Very happy, family's happy, we're happy. I was just never going to turn it down really.

"It's a great honour. It's good to see so many people here as well. I was expecting a fair few people, but it's a 'pinch me' moment. I can't believe his happened."

The mural unveiling happened days after Littler won the 2026 World Matchplay - his 11th PDC major title. Only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen have more.

While Littler could yet end 2026 by winning every major title in a calendar year, Van Gerwen has dropped from fourth to seventh in the PDC's Order of Merit in recent days.

It is the first time he has been outside the world's top four since 2013 - but Littler hopes the Dutchman can rediscover his form to compete with him, as well as Luke Humphries and Gian van Veen, the only three players in the world to have earned more than £1m in prize money in the past two years.

"We're seeing Van Gerwen at the minute who is not playing at his best game - he's down to seventh in the world now is Michael," Littler added.

"Personally, I want Michael to get back to his best. He needs to get back to his best to compete with us."

title: Rangers move a 'dream come true' for South Africa's Makhanya
description: South Africa defender Olwethu Makhanya becomes Rangers' eighth summer signing, joining for an undisclosed fee from Philadelphia Union.
fullText:
South Africa defender Olwethu Makhanya has become Rangers' eighth summer signing, joining for an undisclosed fee from Philadelphia Union.

The 22-year-old centre-back played for the Major League Soccer side 53 times after breaking into the first team last year.

He has signed a four-year deal at Ibrox with the option of a further year.

"I can't even explain how I am feeling right now, it is honestly a big honour and a huge blessing for me to join such a big club with so much history. I can't wait to get started," Makhanya said.

"For me, it has always been a dream to play football in Europe, ever since I was a kid, so to be here is a dream come true."

Makhanya, who started his career with Stellenbosch in his homeland, was rewarded for his impressive club form by being included in South Africa's 2026 World Cup squad.

The defender did not play at this summer's finals, but Rangers boss Derek McInnes feels he has all the tools to thrive in Scotland.

"He's got a lot of athleticism and good potential," McInnes said prior to his side's Scottish Premiership opener at Dundee United on Friday.

"And while he's coming from the MLS, to a different country and a different type of football, we feel he's got the attributes that can cope with that."

title: Minimum 10-match ban for discrimination - FA
description: Players found guilty of discrimination will face a ban of at least 10 matches under strengthened Football Association rules.
fullText:
Players found guilty of discrimination will face a ban of at least 10 matches under strengthened Football Association rules coming in for the new season.

In previous seasons, suspensions ranged from six to 12 matches for 'aggravated breaches' of FA Rule E3.2, which relates to misconduct around references to ethnic origin, colour, race, nationality, religion, sex, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, or disability.

The strengthened sanction, which also applies to managers and individuals in the technical area, is part of the FA's commitment to "delivering a game free from discrimination".

Kick It Out wants tougher sanctions as discrimination hits new high

"While significant progress has been made in recent years, discriminatory conduct continues to be a challenge across the game," an FA statement read.

"Enhanced measured are necessary to tackle this abhorrent conduct."

A sanction above the new standard minimum 10-match suspension may be imposed by a regulatory commission if there are "significant" aggravating factors.

Shorter bans - with a minimum of six matches - may also be considered when there are mitigating circumstances or an individual has admitted the breach at the earliest opportunity. But a six-match ban would now only be considered in those circumstances - rather than being the standard minimum suspension, as it was before.

Individuals who are found to have committed two or more aggravated breaches on separate occasions may face a suspension in excess of 12 matches or time-based suspensions of any duration in "very serious cases".

title: Unbeaten leaders Brave beat bottom side Phoenix
description: Southern Brave continue their unbeaten run with an 24-run win over Birmingham Phoenix at the Utilita Bowl.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Utilita Bowl

Southern Brave 140-3 (100 balls): Bouchier 45 (31); Filer 1-22

Birmingham Phoenix 116-5 (100 balls): Perrin 52 (43); Molineux 2-24

Southern Brave continued their unbeaten run with an 24-run win over Birmingham Phoenix at the Utilita Bowl.

The Hundred leaders completed their fourth consecutive victory as bottom side Phoenix failed to chase a target of 141, finishing on 116-5.

Brave openers Maia Bouchier (45) and Lizelle Lee (43) shared a 68-run partnership after their side was put into bat.

Laura Wolvaardt made an uncustomarily slow 11 from 15 deliveries before being stumped off Alana King, but Jemimah Rodrigues struck an unbeaten 18 as Brave closed on 140-3.

Phoenix openers Davina Perrin and Tammy Beaumont set a reasonable platform, putting on 73 before Beaumont was caught for 22 by Rodrigues off the bowling of Tilly Corteen-Coleman.

The dismissal, shortly after the halfway mark of the innings, stalled the Phoenix chase and matters were made worse when Alice Capsey (eight) and Perrin, who made a 43-ball 52, were caught off Lauren Bell and Sarah Glenn.

Home captain Molineux (2-24) removed Annerie Dercksen and Jemima Spence with consecutive deliveries, while England bowlers Bell (1-16) and Corteen-Coleman (1-19) were economical as Phoenix's challenge petered out.

Brave are now six points clear of second-placed Manchester Super Giants, while Phoenix remain bottom with two wins and a no result from three matches.

title: Elliott ready to take 'second chance' at Liverpool
description: Harvey Elliott discusses his "tough" loan spell at Aston Villa and why he's determined to enjoy his football again at Liverpool.
fullText:
Harvey Elliott says he is ready for a "second chance" at Liverpool and keen to enjoy his football again after a "tough" loan spell at Aston Villa.

Elliott joined Villa last summer on a season-long loan, with a clause in the deal stating Unai Emery's side were obliged to sign him for £35m if he made 10 appearances.

Villa decided early in the season they did not want to trigger that option, meaning the 23-year-old played only nine games and a total of 277 minutes, with Emery describing the situation as "embarrassing for everyone involved".

Elliott returned to Merseyside earlier than planned this summer and has featured in both of Liverpool's pre-season games under new manager Andoni Iraola.

Reflecting on his move to Villa, Elliott said: "I wanted to go and explore something, come out of my comfort zone and do something I thought personally that would take me on as a player again.

"But unfortunately it didn't work out."

Elliott was speaking after Liverpool beat Wrexham 1-0 in a pre-season friendly in New York.

"Now I'm here and it's kind of a second chance, if you want to call it. Especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in, it's another chance to impress and hopefully get in their good books," he said.

"I wish Villa nothing but the very best. I had a lot of love for them and they treated me very well. Unfortunately, the situation happened but it's another learning curve.

"I'm here now and I'm trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad."

Elliott developed in Fulham's academy and made his Premier League debut aged 16, before joining Liverpool in 2019.

He played regularly under then manager Jurgen Klopp but less so in the title-winning season under Arne Slot, making 18 Premier League appearances in 2024-25 before joining Villa, a move that brought challenges.

"Mentally, it was a very tough one, it was a learning curve," said Elliott, who helped Emery's side win the Europa League last season.

"It was an opportunity for me to experience something new, as much as I didn't want to do it, and I don't wish it upon any other player, because it's not nice at all.

"But I have no hard feelings. I'm on the other side of it now. I was able to get through it and achieve something at the end of the season as well, another historical moment for the club, and to be part of that was another great situation."

Looking ahead, Elliott, who won Player of the Tournament as England U21s won Euro 2025 last summer, says he is unsure of his future but will speak to Iraola later in the season.

"Right now, I'm just thinking about making sure I'm physically and mentally 100%, and trying to impress on the pitch," he adds. "I think when it comes to the right time of asking him [Iraola], that's when I'll go and ask.

"Ultimately, it's just down to me. As long as I'm putting in the effort of hard work and the desire on the pitch, then I feel like I have the opportunities to go in and ask.

"But I'm really happy to be back. Since the first day I walked through the door at training, I had a big beaming smile on my face.

"I'm wearing this strip again and putting this shirt on, and I just want to be free, and play as much as I can, and just enjoy it, because sometimes I don't feel like I do it enough. Playing at Liverpool, there's no better feeling."

Joe Gomez will miss the start of the Premier League season after Iraola confirmed the Liverpool centre-back sustained a muscle injury in a 4-2 win over Sunderland on Sunday.

Speaking in Chicago, the morning after Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York, Iraola said: "Joe has a muscle injury. It was quite clear since he complained straight away so he will be some weeks off.

"It's difficult to say - normally one month [out]. If it goes very good, then a little bit less. If it goes bad then a bit more but it's a muscle injury. It's not massive.

"It will be impossible to have him for the start of the season because we are not so far off but it shouldn't be a lot more."

Gomez is still with the squad in Chicago but, with Giovanni Leoni still sidelined and Virgil van Dijk not on the pre-season tour, Iraola has had to resort to Liverpool's younger centre-backs. In more positive news, Jeremy Jacquet is set to make his debut when Liverpool take on Leeds in Chicago on Sunday.

"You've seen in these games that we are pretty thin in the centre-back position," added Iraola.

"The only centre-backs we have right now are Mor [Talla Ndiaye] and Ifeanyi [Ndukwe] who are both 18, just arrived at the club and are doing incredibly well. Luke Chambers played there - he's not a centre-back but he played really well.

"Jeremy is ready to go and we will recover Virgil, but I'm happy that playing against Sunderland and Wrexham with 18-year-old centre-backs, the team has shown composure and solidity at the back and it speaks very well about them."

title: Newcastle captain Guimaraes expected to join Arsenal
description: There is a growing expectation that Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal this summer in a deal worth up to £80m.
fullText:
There is growing expectation that Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal this summer, multiple sources have told BBC Sport.

The Brazil midfielder has made it clear he wants to join the Premier League champions and Arsenal are increasingly confident of signing the 28-year-old.

Guimaraes, who has scored 31 goals in 195 appearances for Newcastle since joining from Lyon in 2022, has been a player of interest to the Gunners all summer.

Arsenal will need to improve the £70m bid they made this month if they are to sign Guimaraes, who is due to return to Newcastle training in the coming days.

Sources insists a new proposal is yet to be submitted, while Newcastle are adamant that formal club-to-club talks over Guimaraes' protracted switch to north London have not taken place.

Challenging times ahead for Newcastle - Shearer

Nevertheless, Arsenal are aiming to agree a deal in the coming days which could reach £80m.

The belief that a move is within reach is not connected to Eddie Howe's decision to step down from his role as Newcastle head coach.

Arsenal were interested in signing Morgan Rogers, who has joined Chelsea for £117m, from Aston Villa - but refused to go higher than their £80m valuation.

It is understood Arsenal were given the opportunity to match Chelsea's offer for Rogers but declined.

Newcastle, meanwhile, now face losing another key player, with Sandro Tonali having joined Tottenham and Anthony Gordon moving to Barcelona.

Howe left Newcastle on Thursday after five years in charge, with Matthias Jaissle, manager of Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli, expected to be appointed his successor.

title: Tonali 'took 10 minutes' to decide to join Spurs
description: Club-record £100m signing Sandro Tonali took "10 minutes" to decide to join Tottenham after meeting manager Roberto de Zerbi.
fullText:
Club-record £100m signing Sandro Tonali took "10 minutes" to decide to join Tottenham from Newcastle after meeting manager Roberto de Zerbi at his home.

The 26-year-old said a shared passion for his boyhood club Brescia played a key role in the move.

De Zerbi grew up a Brescia fan and later played for them, while Tonali started his career there, and that connection helped pave the way for the biggest transfer in Tottenham's history.

"We spoke about Brescia, about the difficult situation facing our club," Tonali said, referring to the bankruptcy of his boyhood side following relegation to Italy's third tier.

De Zerbi texted a mutual friend during last season to ask whether Tonali might be interested in joining Tottenham and was told: "He is open."

His immediate focus was securing Premier League survival and, the day after Tottenham beat Everton to avoid relegation, De Zerbi contacted Tonali about a potential move.

Within 10 minutes, he had received a phone call from the midfielder.

A further meeting at Tonali's home, just outside Brescia, followed as talks progressed.

"Brescia is so small. I had two weeks there and met him two or three times," Tonali said.

Tonali said his connection with De Zerbi stretches back nine years to the coach's spell in charge of Sassuolo, when he wanted to sign him.

That brief reign helped launch De Zerbi's managerial career and began what Tonali described as a "mini-connection".

After their meeting this summer, however, he said he knew "everything" about his future manager.

Sources close to Tonali described how those meetings had captivated him, despite interest from clubs with far stronger recent records than Spurs, who had finished 17th the previous season, allowing Tottenham to pull off a coup.

De Zerbi wants to convince Spence to stay at Spurs

"Honestly, I spoke with another team [also]," Tonali revealed, but in the end the decision to join Spurs was an easy one.

"When you speak with a team, the first impression is a big thing and my impression was very positive.

"When you are happy after a 10-minute chat, it's everything, everything is perfect.

"I spoke with my wife - this was the first thing. We wanted to change our life, but not just for the city, we wanted to change everything. We spoke with two clubs."

Tonali said moving to London represented about 10% of the attraction as he wanted his family to be happy, but said football, De Zerbi and Tottenham's recruitment staff made up the other 90% of his decision.

There was also further discussion about the transfer fee, what it means for him and Newcastle, and how it effectively priced him and his family out of a move back to Italy.

"We had decided to come back in Italy but it was impossible for the money," he admitted, explaining clubs could afford his wages but not the transfer fee.

"England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness, for my family. I spoke with two teams. I understood after 10, 15 minutes that Tottenham would be my next team."

At Spurs, he joins an Italian contingent within the coaching staff and links up with fellow Italy international Destiny Udogie, but he stressed the move was not motivated by any unhappiness during his time at Newcastle.

Unprompted, he said: "Eddie [Howe] was fantastic for me", adding that he wants to maintain a friendship with his former manager - who is also leaving the Magpies - and Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson.

He went on to explain that he wanted "the best deal" for Newcastle because they "deserve everything", while also praising the atmosphere at St James' Park and the passion of the club's supporters.

Although not referenced directly, Tonali served a 10-month ban for breaches of FA betting rules during his time at Newcastle.

His £100m price tag is also something Tonali admits will bring "a lot of pressure", but he insists he will continue to behave as a "normal" Tottenham player and person in his private life.

"I don't know your impression about football players like me, but honestly, I'm a normal person. When I go back to Italy, I go to my family, to my grandma, to my friends. If it is perfect for my family, it is perfect for me," he said.

title: England's Campbell retains Commonwealth weightlifting title
description: England's Emily Campbell produces a record-breaking performance in Glasgow to defend her Commonwealth Games title in the women's +86kg weightlifting.
fullText:
England's Emily Campbell said she wanted to show people "you can love what you do and still be absolutely fabulous while you're doing it" as she retained her Commonwealth Games title in the women's +86kg weightlifting.

The 32-year-old won gold in the heaviest women's division in Birmingham four years ago and she stepped on to the top of the podium again on Thursday after lifting a Games-record total of 278kg.

She also broke the clean and jerk Commonwealth record with 163kg, while she registered a 115kg snatch lift.

"As an athlete, you always want to give your best performance, but the reason I've stayed in the sport so long is because I still genuinely enjoy lifting," Campbell said.

Her total was 25kg more than the weight managed by Malaysia's Siti Aqilah Farhana Draman, who claimed silver with 253kg.

Canadian teenager Etta Mae Love took bronze with a total of 250kg.

Campbell was the final athlete to step on to the platform, with lions braided into her hair, which was dyed bright red in a nod to Team England's colours.

After failing to clear 114kg on her second snatch attempt, she lifted 115kg on her third, a result matched by New Zealand's Tui-Alofa Patolo, who missed out on the medals after managing 130kg in the clean and jerk for a 245kg total.

She did so on her first try, lifting 148kg before increasing the weight to 155kg.

And the cheers in the Armadillo venue reached another level as Campbell lifted a personal best 163kg and danced off the stage in celebration.

"The atmosphere out there was incredible. You couldn't really ask for the crowd to be any louder - I could barely hear myself think," Campbell said.

"Representing England means everything to me. The Commonwealth Games are incredibly special.

"In 2018, I really started believing in myself and realised I could do this. Without those Games, I don't think I'd have achieved what I have now. Whenever I represent my flag, I do it with pride."

Earlier on Thursday, Team England's Cyrille Tchatchet II secured a silver medal in the men's 110kg weightlifting final.

The 30-year-old lifted 166kg in the snatch and 208kg in the clean and jerk for a total of 374kg, which was bettered only by Fiji's Taniela Tuisuva Rainibogi's 378kg.

Tchatchet's success comes 12 years after he defected from Cameroon's team base at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow in 2014, afraid to return to his homeland.

After a period of homelessness in Brighton, Tchatchet rebuilt his life after being granted asylum.

He went on to represent the Refugee Team at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and later became eligible to compete for England.

Twelve years after fleeing the Cameroon camp, Tchatchet stood proudly on the Commonwealth Games podium and later celebrated on stage with his mother, who had travelled from Africa to watch her son compete.

title: Search halted for GB surfer who disappeared in sea
description: Tributes are paid to surfer Arran Strong, after searches for the Brit who went missing off the coast of Portugal were called off.
fullText:
Tributes have been paid to surfer Arran Strong, after searches for the Briton who went missing off the coast of Portugal were called off.

The Autoridade Maritima Nacional (AMN) confirmed to BBC Sport that its search for the 28-year-old, which started soon after he went missing on Monday morning, was halted on Thursday.

Strong, who lived in Portugal, had competed in the World Surf League for 10 years and represented Great Britain at each of the previous two World Surfing Games - finishing as the highest ranked British representative on both occasions.

"Beyond his performances in the water, Arran was a fantastic team-mate, respected competitor and a kind, generous presence whose passion for surfing left a lasting impression on everyone who had the privilege of knowing him," GB Surfing said in a statement on Instagram, external on Tuesday.

"His passing is a devastating loss to our sport and the wider surfing community, and he will be greatly missed.

"Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with Arran's family, friends, team-mates and all those whose lives he touched."

The AMN said it was alerted to Strong getting into difficulties in the water off the Atlantic coast in southern Portugal at 11.33 BST on Monday.

It said: "The young man disappeared at sea while crossing from Monte Clerigo beach to Carrapateira.

"His friend, who was with him, was rescued by a local fishing boat that was nearby."

The friend was Strong's coach, Jose Maria Pyrrait, who said he did not see the moment in which Strong went missing.

Pyrrait wrote on Instagram, external that they had stopped to drink water and take photos, before setting off again with Strong initially in the lead, before the coach overtook him.

"When I stopped to wait, I saw your board drifting about 100 meters away," he wrote.

"I paddled as fast as I could to get there, diving repeatedly looking for you, but we were in a deep area and visibility was very short. I called my partner on land for help, who automatically activated the rescue."

Pyrrait said they had spent another two and a half hours looking for Strong from the boat.

"Arran was like a son to me. From the age of 10 he trained with me and spent weekends and holidays with me, as his mother said, he was like a son of divorced parents. My love for him, was like another son that life gave me," he wrote.

Tributes were paid from many of Strong's team-mates and friends in surfing.

GB Surfing performance coach Luke Dillon wrote: "Hearts so heavy. Fought so many battles and lived life to the fullest always carrying a smile and infectious laugh. Sending love to Arran's family and friends."

Eight-time British national champion Lucy Campbell wrote: "The world is going to miss that smile so much. Sending my love and hugs to you all."

Fellow English women's surfing champion Alys Barton wrote: "Arran, we competed together for so many years and you were always the one encouraging everyone around you.

"Thank you for always smiling, believing in others and lifting everyone up. You will be deeply missed."

Defender Stones joins Inter Milan on free transfer
description: England defender John Stones joins Italian Serie A champions Inter Milan on a free transfer and signs a two-year contract.
fullText:
England defender John Stones has joined Italian champions Inter Milan on a free transfer and signed a two-year contract.

The 32-year-old left Manchester City when his deal expired at the end of June after 10 successful years at the Premier League club.

Stones said he had "lived all my dreams out" after helping City win six Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups, five League Cups, three Community Shields, the Club World Cup and the Uefa Super Cup.

Since he became a free agent, the centre-back has attracted interest from clubs across Europe, including Chelsea and Juventus.

Inter Milan were crowned Serie A champions for the 21st time last season and will start their title defence against newly promoted Monza on Saturday, 22 August.

Former Barnsley defender Stones made 295 appearances for City, scoring 19 goals, after joining from Everton for £47.5m in 2016.

He has won 93 caps and was part of the England squad who finished third at this summer's World Cup, starting the quarter-final victory against Norway and 2-1 semi-final defeat by Argentina.

title: Uefa to boycott World Cups if Fifa plans approved
description: Uefa says "the World Cup is not for sale" after its 55 member associations vote to boycott future tournaments if Fifa and its president, Gianni Infantino, do not back down on their investment proposals.
fullText:
European football's 55 member associations have voted to boycott World Cups if the sport's governing body proceeds with a plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors.

The decision was made at an emergency meeting called to discuss the proposal announced earlier this week by Fifa, which oversees world football.

Uefa, which governs European football, had already made its opposition clear by releasing two damning statements - and that strength of feeling has been reaffirmed.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product," it said on Thursday.

"It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale."

Uefa's boycott would cover all Fifa competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups and Club World Cup, and be triggered if Fifa president Gianni Infantino's proposals are voted through by member associations.

The first time this stance will be tested at a senior tournament is in October, when the Women's World Cup play-offs are due to be held.

It is understood FA chairwoman Debbie Hewitt and chief executive Mark Bullingham were among those to speak during Uefa's meeting, with the atmosphere described as venomous, such was the strength of feeling against the proposals.

Despite being one of eight Fifa vice-presidents, Hewitt had no knowledge of the discussions that Infantino had been having regarding the proposals.

Fifa offers $40m if nations back controversial plan

Is World Cup sell-off plan a step too far by Infantino?

Courting controversy and befriending Trump - Fifa's 'unlikely saviour'

Fifa wants to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors will be able to buy stakes in it.

It said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

The plan needs to be passed by a vote of Fifa's 211 members.

Infantino has written to them saying they will receive $40m (£30m) if they back his controversial proposal. He has set a deadline of 19 September for federations to accept his plans if they want to access an initial $20m (£15m).

In a video released by Fifa on Wednesday, Infantino defended the plans, calling them "an offer, not an obligation".

If approval is granted, Fifa says Thrive Eternal is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Fifa sources have told BBC Sport there has been no discussion over Infantino, or anyone else, becoming chief executive of FFE.

The White House said it had "nothing" to say on Infantino's proposals "at the moment".

In a statement released after Thursday's meeting, which was held virtually and chaired by president Aleksander Ceferin, Uefa said it and its 55 member associations "stand as one".

"We unanimously and unequivocally reject Fifa's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors," it said.

On Wednesday, Uefa had accused Fifa of using football "to enrich themselves and their friends".

Its statement on Thursday was even more damning, calling it "irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret" and "without any meaningful consultation" with those who steward the game.

It added: "This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of Fifa's duty as the custodian of world football.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences.

"This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation - an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

While Uefa only accounts for a quarter of Fifa's membership, it does include most of the world's most successful teams.

Six of the eight quarter-finalists - including winners Spain - at this summer's World Cup were European. In the 2022 and 2018 editions, the figures were five and six respectively.

Of the 23 World Cups to have taken place to date, 13 have been won by European countries. The other 10 have been won by South American sides.

Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister said Fifa's proposals posed a "genuine existential threat to the game".

The former Wales international told BBC Radio Wales she hoped boycotts would not happen, adding: "I feel optimistic they won't, because the reality is the powerhouse of world football is Europe."

Speaking to Radio 4's PM programme, McAllister said there was "real unity" among Uefa members and an "easy consensus over the need to take the strongest possible action given the existential threat that the Fifa proposal poses to our sport".

She added: "The reality is we had no choice other than to issue a threat commensurate with this dreadful, catastrophic proposal that has been rushed through with no due diligence, no proper governance and no consultation."

Uefa and PM criticise Infantino World Cup plan

Infantino tells Fifa critics to 'meditate, pray or watch football'

A Football Association spokeswoman said England stood "shoulder to shoulder" with its European colleagues and "fully support the collective view".

She added: "We oppose Fifa's plans - the Fifa World Cup belongs to football and always will."

The Scottish FA added its support, saying its board "agrees unequivocally with the concerns raised by all members over the manner in which these proposals have been issued, and deadline set, without a full consultation process or consideration to good governance".

Scottish FA president Mike Mulraney is also the chair of Fifa's finance committee.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: "This is a principled decision that we strongly support. Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It's time to take a stand to protect our game."

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham criticised the plans on Tuesday, saying going ahead with the idea would mean Fifa had "sold out".

Ronan Evain - executive director of Football Supporters' Europe - told the BBC that Uefa's stance was "very impressive" and a "proper show of force".

He added: "It is the response that football needed - it is the response Gianni Infantino deserved."

Prior to Uefa's announcement, Concacaf, which covers North and Central America and hosted this year's World Cup, said in a statement: "We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process."

The Asian Football Confederation said it was "disappointed" it had not been consulted before the plans entered the public domain.

The Confederation of African Football said its president Dr Patrice Motsepe would host a meeting of its executive committee next week to "assess and evaluate" the proposals.

The World Leagues Association (WLA) asked Fifa to withdraw its project and the Premier League, which is a WLA member, said it "wholeheartedly endorses" that view.

At this stage, there is a lot we do not know.

Fifa has been asked for a response to Uefa's statement. We do not know how it - and Infantino - will react.

We do not know what the implications will be for the Women's Under-20 World Cup, which is due to be held in Poland from 5 September - before Fifa's 19 September deadline for associations to claim an initial $20m payment by 1 January.

We also do not know what impact Thursday's news will have on Fifa's stated aim to bank the first tranche of 'private investment' cash by the end of October.

"I think on this occasion, Infantino's got to back down," former FA chairman David Bernstein told BBC Sport.

"This deal is not acceptable. If they want to raise capital, there's other, better, ways of doing it.

"In a normal organisation, if he has to back down on something of this magnitude, it would probably mean he'd be shown the door.

"But Fifa is not a normal organisation. If he has the support of enough of the national associations he will continue."

Without some sort of resolution, Uefa would be outside the global governance of the game.

However, Bernstein does not think it will come to that.

"I can't believe in the long term there will be a schism because it would be a lose-lose for everybody," he said.

"Fifa can't afford not to have European nations play in their competitions and frankly, Europe, also can't really afford not to be part of it."

There is no doubt in my mind this story equals that of the European Super League in being the biggest football has had to deal with.

Transfers are huge, but ESL and now this go to the very heart of what makes football the game it is and the structures that underpin it.

The logical conclusion to the involvement of private investment in Fifa competitions is that, eventually, they will be expanded, both in terms of size and frequency. That squeeze on the calendar would be felt all the way down the pyramids domestically and affect the structure of the game in every single country.

Uefa, which has been criticised itself for expanding its club competitions, knows it has the power to stop the Fifa plan.

A World Cup without European teams would rob it of three out of four semi-finalists from this summer's competition and six of the eight quarter-finalists. Three of the four semi-finalists in the last Women's World Cup were European. Three of the four semi-finalists in last year's Club World Cup were European.

If there are no European participants it is impossible to imagine Fifa generating the amount of revenue commercially needed to pay the sums it is offering.

It cannot be overstated how huge this story is.

title: Pembina Pipeline earnings in focus: Can momentum sustain?
Challenging times ahead for Newcastle - Shearer
description: MOTD pundit and Newcastle United legend Alan Shearer explains why he is worried about what will happen next at his old club after the departure of manager Eddie Howe.
fullText:
Thank you, Eddie Howe. You gave me the best day of my life as a Newcastle fan.

Whatever the reasons are for him leaving the club, I think every supporter of my age or younger - and I am 55 - would say the same.

Eddie will always be a legend in the eyes of the Geordie public for ending our long wait for a major trophy with that epic day he gave us at Wembley when we won the Carabao Cup in 2025.

I had craved that moment for my entire life. I had been to Wembley before as a Toon player and I had been there before as a Toon fan, and we'd all had the same feeling of walking away empty-handed.

He will be remembered for changing that, and we have to say a massive thank you for everything else he has done since he took charge in November 2021, when the club were 19th in the Premier League, five points adrift of safety after 11 games.

Eddie kept us up that year, then finished fourth, seventh and fifth in the next three seasons, with some amazing nights in the Champions League along the way. He did a brilliant job.

The best way of showing how far we have come under him is that we finished 12th last season and it was a disappointment, but I would not blame him for that, either.

What happened last summer massively hindered Newcastle, with Alexander Isak leaving and the club missing out on their main transfer targets.

Unfortunately, that trend has continued this year. I would not be surprised if it influenced Eddie's thinking about whether to stay or go, and it also makes me worry about what will happen next.

Speaking purely as a fan, I think we have to get ready for a tough season and some very challenging times ahead.

The timing of Eddie's exit is the biggest surprise for me - three weeks into pre-season, and with only three weeks to go until the Premier League starts again.

I don't know exactly what has gone on behind the scenes for this to happen now but I guess, from his point of view, he was seeing his best players being sold - first Isak, then Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer - and with speculation over captain Bruno Guimaraes' future too.

He has probably thought it was a tough enough job anyway, but it is just getting tougher.

You cannot keep on selling your best players and then hope to be in contention at the top of the table - I hope I'm wrong but it is probably inevitable that Bruno will be next to leave.

Whatever Bruno's intentions were before, when Eddie was in charge, then he must look now and think well, we are selling our stars and now the manager, who he clearly had a great rapport with, has gone too.

It's not just the players leaving that is a bad look, it is seeing a series of attempted signings fail to get over the line as well.

Hugo Ekitike, Johan Manzambi and Victor Munoz all went to Liverpool or Aston Villa ahead of Newcastle in the past 12 months and now it also looks like James Trafford has chosen Leeds instead.

That's something else that Eddie has maybe looked at, because there has to be a reason why Newcastle are not getting so many of their targets.

Losing the manager on top of all this is a huge blow, especially a high-calibre one like Eddie who is going to get some huge job offers from home and abroad off the back of his achievements at St James' Park.

I think even someone really experienced would find the situation a difficult one and Matthias Jaissle, who is expected to get the job, is only 38.

While he has been successful with Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia, you cannot really compare that to working in the Premier League, which is a completely different beast.

Take a step back and, whether we like it or not, we can all see what is happening with all the ins and outs at Newcastle. Whatever statements come out of the club, it is clear the landscape has changed.

It is a changing football club - in terms of its owners' aims and ambitions and their transfer strategy, which all seem massively different to the way they were even three years ago.

Back then the sky seemed to be the limit, and the talk was about competing with the very best.

Now, the approach seems to be to sell their best players and replace them with younger, hungry and up-and-coming prospects. If it was that easy to do it successfully and still compete at the top of the table, then everyone would do it - but it isn't.

The club's spending always had to comply with the Premier League's profitability and sustainability rules but it still felt like the plan was to battle it out for silverware every season.

Go back to the summer of 2023, when Newcastle had just finished fourth and added Tonali, Harvey Barnes and Tino Livramento to a squad already containing Isak, Gordon and Bruno.

It felt like they were ready to challenge for everything, and capable of beating everyone. Howe had made them a horrible team to play against, in the nicest possible way.

Three years on, much of that team has gone and now the manager has too, but it is the whole model which feels the most different.

The goalposts have moved massively from where the club said they wanted to get to, compared to where they are now.

When we won the Carabao Cup, I was hoping it was just the start of something very special, but it seems a lot has changed since then.

Alan Shearer was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

title: England captaincy could be what Root needs - Vaughan
description: Former skipper Michael Vaughan says the England Test captaincy could be "exactly what Joe Root needs" after the 35-year-old is appointed to the role for a second time.
fullText:
Former skipper Michael Vaughan has said the England Test captaincy could be "exactly what Joe Root needs".

Speaking on the Test Match Special podcast, Vaughan said the 35-year-old's return to the role, having led the team from 2017 to 2022, might prove to be motivation in the later stages of his career.

"I just wonder from Joe's perspective if he needed this to get that real enthusiasm to get up every morning to play Test match cricket," said Vaughan.

"The amount of cricket that he's played, I just wonder whether he needed this little trigger, this little motivational tool.

"He hasn't got that many of his close friends in the team any more, a lot of his team-mates have retired or moved on, so maybe this is exactly what Joe Root needs as well."

Root returns to the captaincy under the charge of interim head coach Marcus Trescothick after Brendon McCullum was sacked, before New Zealander Stephen Fleming takes over the Test leadership for this winter's tour of South Africa.

He stepped down as captain in 2022 after a 10-wicket loss to West Indies, their ninth match without a win, citing the "toll" and "impact" the role had on him.

However, Vaughan stated he believed Root had been dealt a "dodgy hand" during his time as Test captain.

"Around the time he was appointed England were trying to win the 50-over World Cup and all the England eggs were put in the white-ball basket," said Vaughan.

"Then Covid struck. None of us would know how hard it would be to captain in a Covid time - Joe had to do that.

"That Caribbean tour where it came to an end, it looked like a job that was a little bit too far for him. He's a little bit older, a little bit wiser. I think Stephen Fleming will help out with a lot of the stuff that some captains get drained by - organising the dressing room and making sure the tactical side of the team is in good order.

"I just think in terms of his motivation and in terms of what is left for Joe Root to achieve in the game, of course there's a few runs to get past Sachin [Tendulkar's all-time Test run-scoring record] but if he can be an Ashes winner next year, a world leader in runs he's scored in Test cricket, you can't ask for a more perfect career."

Stumped podcast: New era for England as Stephen Fleming appointed Test coach

Fleming has been appointed on a four-year deal that will mean he coaches England in the next two Ashes series, and Vaughan said managing director Rob Key has selected a "very experienced" option.

Former England Test coach Andy Flower was initially linked with the role, but Royal Challengers Bengaluru and London Spirit coach ruled himself out of the process.

Fleming joins after leaving Chennai Super Kings this month, having coached the Indian Premier League (IPL) franchise for the past nine seasons.

"Andy Flower, I think from what I've read is the one that they wanted. He turned that down so it was like 'OK, how do we get the next best?'" Vaughan said of Fleming.

"Some will say he's not coached in red-ball cricket but you've got a very experienced manager, very experienced coach who's been around the modern game with Chennai Super Kings over the course of the last few years.

"He was a very, very good captain back in the day, a very good tactician, renowned for being a really good man-manager.

"Having McCullum still as the white-ball coach and then having someone coaching the Test team who doesn't know McCullum, that could have been really tricky.

"I think Stephen Fleming has been brought in for that reason - he's obviously very close to McCullum.

"They needed someone who could work with McCullum because someone that doesn't know Baz and his style, I think it could have got very, very messy."

Fleming, who retired from playing in 2009, has a wealth of experience in Test cricket, making 111 appearances for New Zealand, scoring 7,172 runs with an average of 40.06 in the middle order.

McCullum was known for promoting an aggressive form of cricket, dubbed Bazball by fans and the media, but Vaughan said Fleming will have to make changes to England's style and technique.

"I'm kind of sick and tired of talking about England's style of play. The style of play I want to see is England winning," Vaughan added.

"Whatever that style is on that given day, session, hour, England have to play the right style of cricket that wins games of cricket.

"We can only talk about talent and the gulf of talent in English cricket for so long - they've got to start winning games of cricket and winning trophies now.

"The one thing this Test team needs is coaching the technical side of batting.

"How many of them can look themselves in the mirror and when Michael Neser, Matt Henry, Scott Boland bowls that good length just on or around that off stump, can play a controlled forward defence shot?

"They won't like saying it and they won't like talking about technique, but technique wins Test match cricket and the technical side of England's players and batting has been found wanting.

"So it's all right putting a good leader of the group, but I also think they need one or two changes in the backroom team to make sure these players are getting really well coached as well."

title: WNBA gameday discussion: The latest Liberty vs. Aces matchup is a reminder that this league still belongs to Breanna Stewart and A’ja Wilson
description: Breanna Stewart and A’ja Wilson remain the queens of the WNBA.
fullText:
What remains one of the WNBA’s most compelling rivalries resumes on Thursday night in Sin City: New York Liberty vs. Las Vegas Aces (10 p.m. ET, Prime Video).

Neither team occupies the superteam heights they occupied when this rivalry first launched during the 2023 season.

Despite their status as defending champions, the Aces’ dominance is now pocked with inconsistency, largely due to their lack of depth. After failing to repeat as champs, the Liberty looked for an injection of new energy over the offseason, only to instead become beset by an athleticism deficit that has been compounded by injuries.

And yet, Liberty vs. Aces will always intrigue because for two reasons: Stewie and A’ja.

Stew’ja still are the definitional stars of this league. Their shared status only has been confirmed by their recent performances, where their teams have been as dependent as ever on their absolute brilliance in order to earn wins.

A’ja Wilson and Breanna Stewart have statistically been the WNBA’s two best players this season, and it's no surprise both have continued that dominance throughout July.

Here’s a look at their numbers this month as they prepare for a highly anticipated showdown against each… pic.twitter.com/UUuBEJoXQY

— I talk hoops 🏀 (@trendyhoopstars) July 29, 2026

After New York suffered through a four-game losing streak, Breanna Stewart seemingly decided that she would do whatever it took to lift the Liberty out of their rut.

First, she dropped a 33-point and 10-rebound double-double in a win over the Dallas Wings, playing 42 minutes in the overtime affair. Then, she battled her way to 20 points and nine boards as New York escaped against the Chicago Sky. In the Liberty’s first post-All-Star game, she filled the stat sheet for 29 points, seven assists, four rebounds, four steals and three blocks to get the win over the Los Angeles Sparks.

Increasing the lead 👏

Breanna Stewart calls her own number as she scores on consecutive possessions and forces a timeout call!

NYL-LAS | League Pass 
Tap to watch: https://t.co/sl0hN0tCOl pic.twitter.com/SlGLvSq6at

The season-long leader in wRAPM (regularized adjusted plus-minus) according to Help the Helper, as well as databallr’s RAPM calculation, Stewart has been, at least according to advanced metrics, the most impactful player in the WNBA this season.

The Liberty’s struggles have demanded that Stewie shine, and she has. And of late, her star has been even brighter.

Star power, of course, has become synonymous with A’ja Wilson.

And A’ja understands that with great power comes great responsibility, or accountability. That’s something the four-time MVP consistently expressed in ESPN’s Life in the W documentary. Last season, Wilson, despite her individual excellence, owned the Aces’ struggles, and made it her mission to fix them. Wilson’s acute understanding of the expectations that come with her indvidual achievements and accolades produced title No. 3 for the Aces.

This season, again, is asking a lot of A’ja. And she is, once again, delivering.

Amongst Vegas’ overall uneven performances of late, she is a guarantee.

In a blowout victory over the Toronto Tempo, Wilson nearly put up a point a minute, scoring 26 points in 28 minutes on über-efficiency. When the Aces fell short against the Washington Mystics in DC, she still poured in 38 points, grabbed seven boards, dished five assists, swiped three steals and swatted two shots. Out of the All-Star break, it was more of the same, with a 28-point and 14-rebound double-double in a win over the Portland Fire.

Everywhere on the floor 😮‍💨

A'ja Wilson finished with 28 PTS on 7-of-10 shooting, 14 REB, 4 AST and 2 STL in another dominant performance to power the Aces to the win!#WNBASeason30 pic.twitter.com/cKOFMjsjJG

All that production has padded A’ja’s lead at the top of ESPN Analytics’ MVP ladder, with Wilson having accumulated 123.8 net points, more than 20 points more that second place.

So, the winners of the last four WNBA MVP awards, as well as six of the last eight, deservedly take center stage on Thursday night.

For all their issues, the Liberty have enjoyed two of their best performances of the season against the Aces. Before surviving against the A’ja-less Aces to win the Commissioner’s Cup, the Liberty, powered by 15 second-half points from Stewie, secured an 11-point win in Vegas.

Will the matchup with a familiar foe again produce a favorable outcome for Stewie and the Liberty? Or, in true rivalry fashion, will A’ja and Aces reclaim the advantage?

In the comments, let us know what you expect to see from the Liberty, Aces, Stewie and A’ja, as well as the other stars involved, on Thursday night.

title: Maresca has an eye for detail, says Semenyo
description: Antoine Semenyo says City’s players are enjoying Enzo Maresca’s first couple of weeks at the helm. Men's Team I’m looking forward to seeing what Maresca achieves here, says Wright-Phillips Mares...
fullText:
Antoine Semenyo says City’s players are enjoying Enzo Maresca’s first couple of weeks at the helm.

Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola as boss earlier this summer and is approaching the end of his second week on the training ground.

After seven days at the City Football Academy, the Blues have now flown out to Hong Kong where we are preparing to face Inter in a 12:30 (UK) kick-off this Saturday.

Following that, we’ll travel on to Seoul to play a K League All Stars side and Atletico Madrid, completing preparations for the Community Shield and the Premier League season.

All three games in Asia are live on mancity.com and our official app globally for CITY+ subscribers.

Ahead of that, Semenyo says the City squad are getting to grips with Maresca’s demands.

“Very good, very detailed,” he said about the manager’s training sessions.

“He’s got an eye for detail and he wants everything to be right, which is quite similar to Pep. That’s good for us as players so we’ve enjoyed it so far.”

City were greeted into Hong Kong by a huge crowd outside the hotel and have since got to see some of the best of the city, including a spectacular floating patch in the iconic harbour.

Semenyo says seeing that support reminds the players of the passion for City all around the world.

“The club are global and have a lot of fans,” he began.

“Getting to the hotel from the airport and seeing so many people welcoming us shows the great support we have out here and we look forward to playing in front of them.”

City’s clashes with Inter and Atletico Madrid could well be a prelude to Champions League ties in the coming season and Semenyo says ties like this add an extra edge to pre-season.

“It prepares the players here for the season ahead,” said Semenyo.

“There’s a lot of tough teams in the Premier League and Champions League and Inter and Atletico are two of those so we know that playing those at this stage is a good test for us.”

Since joining City in January, Semenyo has already played 27 times for the Blues and been to the World Cup with Ghana.

However, he insists he’s ready to go as the new campaign nears.

“My body feels good. I like to think I’m well rested,” said Semenyo.

“The manager gave me a couple of weeks to relax and reset so I’m happy to be back with the boys and looking forward to the new season.”

We start in Hong Kong against Italian champions Inter on Saturday 1 August, with kick-off at 12:30 (UK).

After that, we go to Seoul to play a K League All-Stars side on Wednesday 5 August and then Atletico Madrid on Sunday 9 August. Both games begin at 12:00 (UK).

title: Usman Nurmagomedov welcomes ‘little short’ guy Archie Colgan to try and wrestle him: ‘He’s not going to win’
description: Usman Nurmagomedov isn’t afraid to grapple with Archie Colgan in their title fight
fullText:
Usman Nurmagomedov has been one of the most dominant fighters in the PFL but much like his coach and cousin Khabib Nurmagomedov, there’s always going to be certain stylistic matchups that makes it look like he’s vulnerable.

Throughout Khabib’s illustrious career, the question always came up ‘what happens if he faces a dominant wrestler?’ The former UFC lightweight champion answered by putting together a perfect 29-0 record before retiring from the sport to focus on coaching.

Now it’s Usman’s turn to provide his own answers as he takes on former college wrestler turned top lightweight contender Archie Colgan in his latest title defense. But don’t expect the reigning PFL lightweight king to show any fear going up against another wrestler in his latest title defense.

“He’s a little short, uncomfortable fighter,” Nurmagomedov said about Colgan when speaking to MMA Fighting. “He’s wrestling very well but I’m from Dagestsan. I can wrestle, I can grapple, I can do Muay Thai. I can do anything.  Whatever he will compete with me, I am going to be better at. All respect for Archie and his team. He’s not going to win.

“I don’t think he’s going to take me down. This is very hard to take me down, to be honest. I know how I have to fight with little short guys. I always love to fight with the little short guys. I have a longer reach. I can control everything.”

While the wrestling question is going to come up often leading into this main event clash, Nurmagomedov is quick to point out that he’s not wrestling Colgan — they are fighting. Nurmagomedov is confident he can match Colgan anywhere on the feet or on the ground and if they want to settle the wrestling debate there’s another way that can happen.

“I think I’m going to grapple with him, too,” Nurmagomedov said. “I think I can take him down. My wrestling is not bad. We can do it like this. I’m going to beat him or knock him down, I know I’m going to beat this guy. For the people if they want to see who is better in the wrestling, we can do it in RAF.”

If anything, Nurmagomedov really hopes that Colgan can bring out the best in him because that’s what he always wants when he’s going out to defend his title.

“I think I have a big potential inside of me,” Nurmagomedov said. “I have very big ambitions. I just need somebody with who I can show this for the people.”

As far as the future goes, Nurmagomedov is undoubtedly going to be bombarded with questions about what comes next as he competes on Friday’s PFL card on the final fight of his contract.

There’s been heavy speculation that Nurmagomedov plans to leave PFL and sign with the UFC, especially now that his teammate and friend Islam Makhachev left the lightweight division to compete at welterweight instead.

Nurmagomedov hasn’t made any decisions yet and he’s doing his absolute best to shut out all the noise until after his fight.

He knows getting distracted is the perfect recipe for disaster if he’s not putting his full focus on Colgan and the fight directly ahead of him.

“Archie, he’s undefeated,” Nurmagomedov said. “You can’t stay like this for a long time [being undefeated] if you’re not in the top five. That’s why he’s the No. 1 contender and of course, he wants to take everything what I have.

“I don’t want to look ahead and thinking about the future for my career. I have a fight. I have a name. We’re going to fight. I have a fight and we have to do this.”

title: Battle of the Hawgs – Preview for the Chicago Bears’ Training Camp Battle at Center
description: Our guy @EDuerrwaechter gives his takes on the Bears’ upcoming battle at Center.
fullText:
As we’ve finally made it to Training Camp for the Chicago Bears, and there shall be a slew of competitions at multiple positions across the roster. Most recently, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed there will be such a contest for the starting job at Center. The two contestants are veteran Garrett Bradbury and rookie Logan Jones.

Regardless of who ultimately wins the job this season, all signs point to Logan Jones becoming *the* guy at Center for 2027 and beyond. That being said, the youngster from Iowa will have his chance to unseat the veteran in Bradbury, who was acquired this offseason via trade from the New England Patriots. I firmly believe this is the most underrated competition to watch at Halas Hall this year.

Previous team(s): NC State Wolfpack; Minnesota Vikings; New England Patriots

The former 18th overall pick of the 2019 NFL Draft has started in all 105 career games he dressed for between the Vikings and the Patriots. Just coming off a Super Bowl run with the Patriots he was also in a similar situation when they selected current starter Jared Wilson with the 95th overall pick and played him at guard during his rookie season. While there was no competition during training camp in Foxborough, he cemented himself as a key cog for an efficient group which spearheaded one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Nothing spectacular, just solid. And solid is all the Bears need at Center for the time being.

Naturally, the Bears didn’t plan for this transition to happen so soon in the first place. Pro Bowler Drew Dalman was just 27 years old and coming off his best season of his career before abruptly retiring in the spring. This caused Ben Johnson and Ryan Poles to scramble for both an immediate and long-term solution to their center position on relatively short notice. Ultimately, they pivoted towards a trade that landed Garrett Bradbury. He now reunites with a former NC State teammate in All-Pro Guard and reigning Protector of the Year Joe Thuney as well.

What I will point out is that offensive line coach Dan Roushar has only seen one rookie in his career take the mantle as his team’s starting center – Erik McCoy in 2019. Then again, Garrett Bradbury himself started in every game as a rookie too. The center position is by far the most difficult to learn as you have to master both calling protections and your techniques between snapping the ball and identifying the first threat from inside. A team pursuing their own run at the Super Bowl, like the Bears, may not have the appetite for a learning curve at center.

Previous Team(s): Iowa Hawkeyes

Here we have the young challenger to the Bears’ job at Center. While he doesn’t have any experience as a pro just yet, there is a ton of buzz surrounding this latest selection from the OL factory known as Iowa Hawkeye brand football. And it’s not just because the jersey number (54) has returned to the Bears’ lineup.

The Bears picked him as the first center to hear their name called during the 2026 NFL Draft at selection number 57 overall. A spot that has seen great history for the Bears from previous draft classes, including one Devin Hester. The Heinz 57 sponsored product brings with him an excellent set of physical tools anchored by sound technique and a keen awareness for how protections are set. He was named the recipient of the 2025 Rimington Trophy as the nation’s top ranked center in NCAA football as well.

A player most frequently brought up as a pro comparison for Logan Jones – Drew Dalman. Their physicality and athleticism from the center position are reminiscent to each other, where you can see both players pulling naturally when called upon in protection or road paving. The Bears had Logan Jones as their top choice at Center from the start of the process and pounced on him when he was still there in the second round.

There have not been a ton of rookies to start and finish a full season at center for the Bears in recent history. The last such occurrence was in 2016 when Cody Whitehair was kicked inside shortly after the surprise signing of All-Pro Guard Josh Sitton. Even Olin Kruetz himself started just one game during his rookie season. Yet I’d argue the Bears haven’t drafted a pure center who’s nearly as good as Logan Jones is in quite some time.

From the moment his name was called there always was a chance for him to compete for a starting job this year instead of waiting until Garrett Bradbury’s eventual departure. When the pads come on starting next Monday, his opportunities will open up. I’d expect this competition to last all the way until the second preseason game.

Even though Garrett Bradbury is listed as a few pounds heavier, their wingspans are almost identical, with Garrett Bradbury being measured at 1.94m (6ft 4-1/2in) and Logan Jones at 1.93m (6ft 4in). I would almost be willing to bet that Logan Jones will be at or around 305 pounds solid by the end of this season as well.

This is almost self-explanatory, as we have an 8-year veteran with 105 career starts going against a rookie. That experience will come in handy as the Bears look to get into an offensive groove as quickly as possible.

Logan Jones is almost as perfect of a fit for what both Ben Johnson and Dan Roushar want at center that you can possibly imagine. While Bradbury is no slouch himself with a 4.92 forty compared to Jones’ 4.90 forty, Jones wins hands-down in the 3-cone time with a stunning 7.35, in comparison to a respectable 7.41 by Bradbury. What’s more is Jones’ athleticism pops on film as he can run any protection asked of him, while Bradbury has occasionally struggled when tasked to pull or slide in protection. Jones is extremely powerful at the point of attack as well.

What I’m looking at here is seeing who can be counted on right this second to line up and play center for the Bears if a game were happening at the time this article was published. Garrett Bradbury has all the experience, technical expertise, and knowledge of protections to identify the first threat before the ball is snapped. His previous chemistry with Joe Thuney is a plus as well. It is a very tall task for any rookie to line up at center during week one.

Much like the experience question above, this is blatantly obvious. Never mind the 7-year age difference between each player, their contracts also are drastically different. Garrett Bradbury signed a revised deal following his arrival to Chicago which amounts to 1-year and $4.7M. Out of the total value $3.7M is fully guaranteed with an additional $1M moved to what’s called Not Likely to be Earned (NLTBE) incentives. Logan Jones is on the standard 4-year rookie contract with a pre-slotted $8.47M and a $2.12M annual average.

Yes, I did literally just say I’d expect Garrett Bradbury to get the nod if a game happened while I’m sitting at my desk typing this article. However, if Logan Jones performs well enough during training camp, then I cannot see Ben Johnson turning down a chance for the future to begin right away at center. I’m not simply saying he needs to be adequate – he needs to be outstanding for him to unseat Garrett Bradbury. I.E. dominate from the very moment the pads come on. Otherwise, the job will go to Garrett Bradbury, and Logan Jones will wait his turn. Whether that is in 2027 or this season is up to a multitude of factors.

Who do you think opens week one with the starters at center?
